key_insight: The paper shows that exact uniform sampling over permutations can be achieved with variational, connectivity-aware quantum circuits, even on linear nearest-neighbor hardware.
engineering_relevance: This removes the all-to-all connectivity assumption for a key quantum subroutine and lowers exact circuit depth to linear scaling, making hardware-constrained implementations more practical.
method: Build a variational circuit whose gate pattern follows the device interaction graph.
Use controlled-SWAP-based constructions to enforce exact uniform permutation statistics.
Prove a linear-depth O(n) implementation on nearest-neighbor topologies and analyze a Beneš-like architecture.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact uniformity with quadratic circuit size and linear depth O(n) on linear nearest-neighbor layouts, plus a proof that Beneš-like circuits cannot be uniform for any parameter choice.
watch_item: Exact uniformity depends on carefully designed controlled-SWAP constructions and topology-specific compilation, so practical performance may still be limited by hardware noise and gate overhead.
paper_title: Variational Approach for Uniform Quantum Permutation Generators
